competition_series: FSG (Formula Student Germany) primary; also FS Austria (FSA), FS Spain, FS East, FS Czech
summary: TUfast is one of the earliest Driverless entrants in Formula Student, tracing its DV program to a 2016 concept paper and fielding its first driverless car (db017) in 2017 by converting an existing 2015 electric platform (eb015). The team ran separate db-series driverless cars alongside its EV/combustion cars through 2020, then pivoted in 2021-2022 to a combined hybrid EV+DV platform (xb-series) that competes in both classes with one car. Results climbed steadily from mid-pack (db019, 9th FSG overall 2019) to a 4th place FSG Driverless Cup finish (xb022, 2022) and a first DV discipline win (xb023, 1st Driverless Acceleration, FSG 2023), culminating in a 1st place overall DV finish at FS Spain 2025. Public documentation is strong on sensor/compute hardware and competition results per car generation but weak on EBS actuator specifics, cost, and internal schedule slips.

ramp_phases: Named informally by generation rather than explicit phase labels: (1) 'db-series' driverless-only mule/prototype cars (db017-db020, 2017-2020, built alongside separate EV/combustion cars), (2) transitional combined-entry year (eb020, 2021), (3) 'xb-series' unified hybrid EV+DV platform (xb022 onward, 2022-present), replacing the need to build two separate cars each season.
what_slipped: [uncertain] No public source documents specific schedule slips, delays, or missed milestones for TUfast's DV program. The multi-year climb from a 9th-place finish (db019, 2019) to a 4th-place Driverless Cup finish (xb022, 2022) and only a single-discipline win by 2023 (xb023) suggests the full-stack (perception+SLAM+planning+control) maturity took roughly 5-6 seasons longer than the mechanical/EBS side, but no team source explicitly names this as a slip.
platform_prerequisites: Yes - TUfast's first driverless car (db017, 2017) was explicitly built by converting an existing 2015 electric vehicle (eb015) rather than a ground-up chassis, and later db-series cars were revamps of prior-year DV cars (db018->db019). This EV-conversion-first approach was used repeatedly until the 2022 xb-series unified the EV and DV programs into one car.
ebs_design: [uncertain] db018 is documented as using a 'pneumatic braking system' with 'direct drive steering' and CPU-based control, consistent with the standard FSG/DT.3.2 approach of independent pneumatic circuits pressurizing brake master cylinders. No public source gives TUfast's specific EBS actuator model, accumulator pressure/volume, or number of independent actuators.
steering_actuation: [uncertain] db018 documented as 'direct drive steering'; later cars (xb022/xb023) use 'curvature-based steering control' as the control-software layer, but no source specifies the actuator motor, gearing, mounting location, or DT.2.2 decoupling mechanism.
brake_actuation: [uncertain] not documented separately from the EBS pneumatic system
chassis_impact: Each db-series generation was a CFRP monocoque revamp of the prior car; from 2022 onward the xb-series merged the previously separate EV and DV chassis programs into a single hybrid-capable monocoque, which is itself a significant chassis-impact decision (one car must carry both DV sensor/compute mass and full competitive EV performance).
compute_platform: [uncertain] Only a single secondary source (formulastudent.de team page) cites an 'NVIDIA Jetson Xavier processor' for the 2019-era car; no model is confirmed for db017/db018 or for the xb-series (2022+). No secondary safety MCU is documented.
sensor_suite: db019 (2019, most fully documented year): Hesai Pandar40 LiDAR, IDS UI-5244LE-C-HQ-MB monocular camera, Basler Ace GigE stereo camera, OxTS RT4003 GNSS/INS. xb022/xb023 (2022-2023): Ouster OS1 64-layer LiDAR (camera model and GNSS/IMU models not specified in public sources; team sponsor list includes SBG Systems, a navigation-system supplier, suggesting possible SBG INS use on later cars, unconfirmed). Wheel speed/steering encoder details not documented.
shutdown_circuit_implementation: [uncertain] not documented beyond generic FSG DT.4 compliance assumption
custom_pcbs: Self-developed powertrain electronics are documented across generations: a <3kg lightweight motor controller and BMS (db019), and a fully self-developed SiC inverter, control unit, BMS, and dashboard (xb022/xb023). These are drivetrain PCBs rather than DV-specific PCBs; no DV-specific custom PCB (e.g., safety relay board) is documented.
software_stack: fastSLAM localization with Extended Kalman Filter state estimation (documented for xb022 and xb023); minimal-curvature raceline optimization for global motion planning; local motion planning layered on top; curvature-based steering control combined with slip control and torque vectoring for longitudinal dynamics. Path/track-limit generation reportedly uses a Delaunay-triangulation algorithm ('Urinay', originally built for BCN eMotorsport) that was later adapted/improved for TUfast. A self-developed simulation suite (lap-time sim, multi-body sim, HiL, SiL, MiL, 'YMD' sim) is integrated into a CI pipeline.
perception_approach: [uncertain] LiDAR + camera sensor fusion is implied by the documented sensor suite, but no public source specifies the detection algorithm (e.g., YOLO variant vs. classical LiDAR clustering) or achieved detection range for TUfast specifically.
slam_localization_approach: fastSLAM with Extended Kalman Filter (EKF) state estimation, documented for the xb022 (2022) and xb023 (2023) cars.
planning_approach: Minimal-curvature raceline optimization for global path/speed planning, combined with local motion planning; track-limit/center-line generation reportedly uses the Delaunay-triangulation-based 'Urinay' algorithm, adapted from BCN eMotorsport for TUfast use.
control_approach: Curvature-based steering control combined with slip control and torque vectoring for longitudinal control (documented for xb022/xb023, 4-wheel-drive hub-motor platform). No source specifies whether lateral tracking uses Pure Pursuit, Stanley, or MPC specifically.
simulation_tooling: Self-developed simulation suite covering lap-time simulation, multi-body simulation, Hardware-in-the-Loop (HiL), Software-in-the-Loop (SiL), Model-in-the-Loop (MiL), and a tool referred to as 'YMD' simulation, wired into a continuous-integration pipeline (documented for xb022).
ci_cd_testing: CI is described as running 'multiple simulation pipelines' (lap-time, multi-body, HiL/SiL/MiL) for the xb022 generation; no further detail on test coverage or regression-suite scope is available.
open_source_repos: No TUfast-owned public DV repository was found. TUfast is cited as a downstream user/improver of the 'Urinay' Delaunay-triangulation track-limit algorithm originally developed by BCN eMotorsport (https://github.com/origovi/urinay) - useful as a reference implementation of TUfast's likely planning approach, though not an official TUfast repo.
critical_path_items: [uncertain, inferred] (1) Reliance on converting/reusing prior-year EV or DV chassis rather than clean-sheet builds, which gated each new car on the previous year's platform being finished first; (2) full-stack perception+SLAM+planning maturity, which took roughly five to six seasons (2017-2022) to reach even a 4th-place Driverless Cup finish; (3) the 2021-2022 transition to a single combined EV+DV chassis (xb-series), which required unifying two previously separate engineering programs into one vehicle.
long_lead_procurement: [uncertain] Specific lead times not documented for TUfast. LiDAR units (Hesai Pandar40, later Ouster OS1 64-layer) and the OxTS RT4003 GNSS/INS are the highest-value long-lead sensor items in the documented sensor suite, but no team-specific lead-time-in-weeks figures were found.

validation_strategy: [uncertain] not documented beyond general FSG driverless tech-inspection/EBS-test requirements that apply to all teams
rules_compliance_challenges: [uncertain] not documented in public sources specific to TUfast
documentation_burden: [uncertain, inferred] TUfast scored well on Business Plan/Cost & Manufacturing events in multiple years (e.g., 1st place Business Plan/Cost & Manufacturing at FS Spain 2019), suggesting a mature documentation process, but no specific effort/hours figures for DSF/ASF or design reports were found.
dv_event_results: 2019: FS East 4th overall; FSG 9th overall; FS Spain 2nd overall. 2021: 2nd overall podium at FSG and FS ATA (combined EV+DV entry). 2022 (xb022): FSG 1st Autocross, 3rd Skidpad, 4th Overall, 4th Driverless Cup; FSA 4th Business Plan; FS Spain 2nd Engineering Design; FS East 4th Engineering Design. 2023 (xb023): FSA 2nd overall; FSG 1st Driverless Acceleration. 2025: FS Spain DV 1st overall; FSG DV 4th place. 2026: FS Czech DV 2nd overall (1st Driverless Autonomous, 2nd Engineering Design).

top_mistakes: [uncertain] Not explicitly documented by the team in public sources. Inferred from the results trajectory: running two fully separate EV and DV chassis programs in parallel (db-series, 2017-2020) appears to have diluted engineering resources and is consistent with the team not moving past mid-pack DV finishes until consolidating to a single hybrid xb-series platform in 2022.

team_structure_dv: TUfast overall fields approximately 80 members across 20 nationalities and 8 faculties (with a broader alumni/sponsor network of 1200+). Per the team's own description, the autonomous/DV subteam is responsible for sensor integration, mapping/state-estimation (SLAM), and path/racing-line calculation; it is one of several specialized subteams alongside aerodynamics, powertrain, and statics/business. Exact DV subteam headcount by year is [uncertain] and not published.
budget_estimate: [uncertain] Not disclosed. Known sponsors relevant to the DV/electronics side include Eurocircuits (PCB fabrication), WMH Group Germany (materials), and SBG Systems (navigation systems), but no total or per-year DV budget figures were found.
recommended_sequence: Inferred from TUfast's own history: (1) secure or convert an existing running EV platform rather than building a bespoke DV chassis first (as done with eb015->db017); (2) get a minimal sensor+compute+actuation stack running for straight-line Acceleration first; (3) add LiDAR/camera perception and SLAM/state-estimation for Skidpad (known, closed-loop track); (4) extend planning/control to Autocross and Trackdrive (unknown track, full autonomy); (5) develop and validate the EBS/braking system in parallel so it is ready well before dynamic events; (6) once the DV stack is competitive, consolidate the EV and DV chassis programs into a single hybrid platform (as TUfast did with the xb-series from 2022) to stop duplicating engineering effort across two cars.
applicability_to_24_month_ramp: TUfast's own 2016-concept-to-2017-first-car timeline (roughly 12 months) shows that a first autonomous run is achievable quickly when reusing an existing EV platform, which matches the target team's situation (running EV, ~9 software-focused members). However, TUfast then took roughly five to six additional seasons (2017-2022) to reach even a top-4 Driverless Cup finish, and did not win a single DV discipline outright until 2023 - suggesting the software stack (perception, SLAM, planning, control) is the genuine long pole, not the initial mechanical/EBS integration. For a 24-month window (June 2026-June 2028), the team should: front-load SLAM/perception/planning development in year one while EBS/steering integration proceeds in parallel (as TUfast's roughly-parallel mechanical/software tracks suggest is feasible); avoid TUfast's early mistake of running separate EV and DV chassis programs by designing the DV integration into the existing EV platform from day one; and treat a competitive (top-4) Driverless Cup finish as a multi-year, not single-season, goal even under an accelerated timeline.
